question: When was the First Five-Year Plan launched in India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**1951**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The First Five-Year Plan of India was launched in **1951** and covered the period from 1951 to 1956.
 
• It was based on the **Harrod-Domar Model**, which emphasized investment and savings as the key to economic growth.
 
• The primary focus of the First Five-Year Plan was on **agriculture, irrigation, and energy** to address food shortages and boost rural development.
 
• The plan aimed at achieving a growth rate of **2.1%** annually, but India successfully achieved a growth rate of around **3.6%**.
 
• The Planning Commission, established in **1950**, was responsible for formulating and overseeing the implementation of the Five-Year Plans.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Five-Year Plans in India**

 
 
• India adopted the concept of centralized economic planning inspired by the Soviet Union.
 
• The Planning Commission was established under the leadership of **Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru** to implement the Five-Year Plans.
 
• Each plan targeted specific sectors such as agriculture, industry, and social development based on national priorities.
 
• The Five-Year Plans continued until **2017**, when they were replaced by the **NITI Aayog's Three-Year Action Agenda**.
 
 
 
• **Harrod-Domar Model**
 
 
• This economic model emphasizes the importance of savings and investment in achieving economic growth.
 
• The model assumes that economic growth is directly proportional to the savings rate and inversely proportional to the capital-output ratio.
 
• It was used as a foundational framework for India's First Five-Year Plan.
 
 
 
• **Planning Commission**
 
 
• Established in **1950**, the Planning Commission was tasked with assessing resources and formulating India's Five-Year Plans.
 
• The commission worked under the chairmanship of the Prime Minister and included experts from various fields.
 
• It was replaced by **NITI Aayog** in **2015** to better align with contemporary needs.
 
 
 
• **Focus of the First Five-Year Plan**
 
 
• The plan prioritized **agriculture** due to severe food shortages in the post-independence period.
 
• Key projects included the development of irrigation systems like the **Bhakra Nangal Dam** and energy initiatives.
 
• It also focused on land reforms and rural development to improve livelihoods in the countryside.
